object_description: simple rectangular hall building with a slightly inclined gable roof and a covered forecourt
design_condition: the hall fits into the orthogonal structure of the school complex along a newly created open space axis, with a wide covered forecourt complementing the adjoining break area

positive: The new hall fits into the orthogonal structure of the school complex
Access follows a newly created open space axis with the combined hard court at the top
A varied, partly deliberately staggered sequence of buildings and open spaces results
The wide covered forecourt works as a workspace complementing the adjoining break area
The separable foyer with counter sits in the middle with the two workrooms on both sides
The double hall one floor lower can be overlooked from the gallery
The halls are illuminated by a front window band and skylight bands on the longitudinal facades
The different open space and access levels are connected via parallel stairs and ramps
Separation of work classes and sports activities is possible without special measures
The two workrooms can be easily locked and lessons can also use the workspace in front
All rooms are accessible via tightly and clearly organised access areas
The polyvalent foyer with separable multi-purpose room and gallery meet reasonable expectations
The project is close to the average of all entries in building volume and total cost
The project is designed to be tight and practical in many respects
negative: The proportions of the simple rectangular hall are not comparable to the small-grain surroundings
Little concrete measures can be identified for the design of breaks and playgrounds
The very compact volume probably has slightly higher air spaces under the sloping roof
The exposed aggregate concrete facade appears rather cheap and hardly aesthetically satisfactory
The same applies to roofing with corrugated iron
The western corner extends the already expanded construction area by around 5 metres
The inline court is created with an embankment and is completely hidden from the building
Although apparently single storey the hall still looks like an oversized giant barn
The addition makes only a small contribution to improving the heterogeneous complex
